description.narrative: Objective of the Initiative: The Initiative aims to promote the development of sustainable livelihood models based on green and circular economy approaches, led by women, in A Lưới 1 and A Lưới 2 Communes. This will be achieved by transforming degraded agricultural land into aquaculture and organic medicinal plant cultivation models linked to market demand, thereby increasing household income, protecting the environment, conserving biodiversity, and advancing gender equality Duration: 18 months (from October 1, 2025 to March 31, 2027) Target groups/ beneficiaries Direct Beneficiaries: - 100 community members, mainly women from the Pa Cô, Tà Ôi, and other ethnic minority groups in A Lưới 1 and A Lưới 2 Communes: They will directly participate in livelihood transformation models such as aquaculture and organic medicinal plant cultivation, and receive capacity-building training on sustainable livelihood development based on Nature-based Solutions (NbS) and Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA), market access, and circular economy approaches. - 50 households, mainly ethnic minority households—particularly those struggling to find alternatives to low-efficiency farming systems in the project area: They will be supported to develop alternative livelihood models, benefiting from more stable production and improved income. - Producer groups and households: They will receive technical support to organize production along value chains, strengthen market linkages, and participate in building circular economy models to minimize waste and make use of by-products. - Thành Ân Organic: will benefit from expanded and increased supply of raw materials for its production activities, as well as the upgrading ofproduction lines to improve capacity, reduce fuel costs, andminimize the use of plastic packaging. This contributes to reducing CO₂emissions and plastic waste, while enhancing communication, product promotion, and brand development for the company. Indirect Beneficiaries: - Local communities, particularly in ALưới 1 and A Lưới 2 Communes where the project will be implemented: They will benefit from an improved living environment, protected biodiversity, and have opportunities to adopt sustainable livelihood models if these are scaled up. - Local authorities atvarious levels and social organizations: They will gain effective livelihood models that canbe integrated into National Target Program 1719, OCOP, and sustainable development initiatives in ethnic minority areas. They will also have access to practical evidence to inform policies on livelihoods, environment, and gender equality, while contributing to the strategic direction of developing high-value medicinal plant regions. - Enterprises within the medicinal plant and green agricultural supply chains:They will benefit from a more stable supply of raw materials that meet ecological and social standards, and from the development of sustainable local production areas.

participating-org.narrative: Centre for Social Research and Development (CSRD) is a local non-government organization which is registered with the Hue Union of Science and Technology Associations (HUSTA). CSRD has been registered and operated since 2008. CSRD is based in Hue in the Central Region of Vietnam, and many of the projects have been located in the provinces of Central Region. CSRD also works throughout Vietnam and more broadly in South East Asia on water resources issues because CSRD is the administration centre for the Vietnam Rivers Network (VRN). The CSRD mission is to work towards a better life for all people in Vietnam, particularly for those who are poor and vulnerable, and adversely impacted by Vietnam#s industrial development. The hydropower industry is a current focus because many power plants are planned and many are already operating. CSRD#s approach is to work in partnership with local communities and grass roots groups, and to bring communities together so that they may learn from each other. The organization#s work has been recognized by local and provincial authorities and by the National Union of Science and Technology Associations. CSRD maintains very good relationships with community partners; and has a positive record for achieving specific project outcomes.
